title: Content-priority sieve and staged-decode fallback for load shedding
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Design and implement a request-level 'content-priority sieve' admission layer plus a staged-decode fallback path for graceful degradation under overload. The sieve assigns a cost/priority score using cheap request-side heuristics (payload length, presence of tool calls, streaming requested, user plan tier, inferred latency sensitivity) and routes requests into dynamic priority lanes. If queued latency threatens SLOs, staged-decode fallback attempts progressively cheaper execution paths: cached prefix replay -> abbreviated decode with constrained tokens -> summary-mode using small-model proxy. The goal is to reduce p95 latency and error-budget burn during spikes while preserving signal for evaluation and respecting tenant fairness.
acceptance_criteria: 1) New admission layer computes score within 200us per request in the fastpath. 2) Priority lanes enforce isolation so high-priority lane p95 stays within SLOs when overall cluster load is 85%. 3) Staged-decode paths are exercised in canary traffic with fallbacks documented and metric-tagged. 4) Observability: dashboards for score distribution, fallback-rate, per-tenant degrade_count, and SLO burn linked. 5) Integration tests that simulate a regional failover and ensure behavior degrades to expected grace levels instead of hard errors.
progress_updates: 2025-02-20: Initial ticket created after postmortem for 2025-02-18 surge (incident INC-2025-02-18). Observed high p95 and massive tail-burn for mixed requests.

2025-02-25: Prototype sieve scoring in proxy layer. Basic rules: short payloads + no tool calls -> score 10; tool call present -> score 2; streaming requested -> score 3. Fastpath latency measured 180us in lab (good).

2025-02-28: Design review w/ PM + UX + SRE. PM asked for tenant-visible degrade reason codes; SRE pushed for sampling to preserve eval signals. Added stochastic sampling bucket for 1% of degraded requests to always run full path and log outputs.
2025-03-03: Canary rollout config ready. Load generator scenarios created: content-mix A (chat-heavy), B (long-decode docs), C (tool-call heavy). Observability panels drafted in Grafana.
decisions: Use lightweight heuristics in the edge proxy for scoring to avoid an extra RPC. Keep scoring deterministic for reproducibility.
Implement three priority lanes (high / normal / opportunistic) with elastic token buckets per lane rather than strict queue length limits.
Staged-decode fallback will be implemented in-runtime as a fallback policy that can swap model variants or short-circuit to cached prefix replay.
tradeoffs: Accuracy vs latency: abbreviated decode reduces token fidelity; to mitigate we sample 1% for full responses to monitor regressions.
Complexity vs observability: scoring in proxy reduces latency but increases coupling; we add strong audit logs and request-level trace IDs to trace scoring decisions.
Fairness vs utilization: opportunistic lane may starve low-paying tenants under extreme bursts; we add proportional credit pools and tenant caps to enforce fairness.
monitoring: New metrics: sieve.request_score (histogram), lane.queue_time_ms (p50/p95), staged_fallback.rate (per-second), staged_fallback.by_reason (tags), tenant.degrade_count (counter), slo.burn_rate (per-customer)
Dashboards: 'Sieve Health', 'Fallbacks & Fidelity', 'Tenant Fairness' panels created in /dashboards/reliability/sieve.json
Alerts: p95_queue_time > 250ms for high lane -> trigger paging. fallback_rate > 5% sustained over 5m -> Ops ticket and automatic rollback threshold.
runbook_snippet: If p95 latency for high-priority lane exceeds SLO: 1) Check global headroom and recent failovers in console; 2) If multi-region failover active, reduce cross-region steering weight and enable regional-only fastpath; 3) Increase opportunistic-lane trimming aggressiveness by 20% via runtime flag; 4) Notify product teams and enable verbose tracing for sampled degraded requests.
notes: Must coordinate with Dedicated team for reserved capacity semantics; feature flags will gate rollout per-cluster. Also involves minor billing telemetry changes to record degraded response units for customer-facing quotas.
review_feedback: PM (Liam O'Connor): Add human-readable degrade reason codes surfaced via API response header.
SRE (Maya Chen): Add circuit-breaker tie-in: if remote-region RTT > 300ms, block cross-region fallbacks and prefer local low-fidelity modes.
Design (Sofia Reyes): Ensure UX for 'Why my request was degraded' in Console requests view — link to tickets.
next_steps: Complete runtime PR for staged-decode paths and unit tests (target: 2025-03-12).
Roll canary in us-west-2 with 5% traffic; run content-mix A/B test for 48h.
Add billing signal for degraded units and validate with finance before wide rollout.
Postmortem template for any canary regressions and iterate on scoring heuristics.
